review_notes: Read the whole file and the helper lemmas it uses (wderiv_congr, mderiv_trace, mderiv_smooth, matrix_smooth_mul, wderiv_logdet, closed_dz_symmetry, dz/dzbar/wderiv definitions). Two modest simplifications found. Other proofs (curvature_formula, curvature_contraction_at_one, connection_symmetric) are already reasonably direct. I did not compile anything, so the defeq unfolding of dzbar/curvature behind the first suggestion is assumed. The existing `exact mderiv_trace ...` already relies on the same unfolding.

findings.excerpt:
rw [show dzbar (e i) (dz (e j) (fun y => (K.logDet y:ℂ))) z =
    dzbar (e i) (fun y => (K.connection j y).trace) z from wderiv_congr he _ _]
  exact mderiv_trace
findings.problem: The proof restates a long `dzbar ... = dzbar ...` equation in a `show ... from` only so that `rw` can use `wderiv_congr he _ _`, and then closes with `exact`. The equation is just `wderiv_congr` up to unfolding `dzbar`, so the restatement adds length and a place for the term to drift from the goal without adding any information.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the `rw [show ...]` and `exact` lines with a single transitivity step:
  exact (wderiv_congr he _ _).trans
    (mderiv_trace (K.connection_smooth j |>.contDiffAt (K.isOpen.mem_nhds hz)) _ _)
The two-step shape is then visible in the term itself: first replace `dz (e j) logDet` by the trace of the connection (`he`), then commute the trace with the Wirtinger derivative (`mderiv_trace`). The `change` on line 83 should already put the goal in the form `wderiv ...` that `Eq.trans` needs, since `dzbar` is a reducible-by-delta definition `wderiv Complex.I v f`.
findings.benefit: Removes a six-line-wide restated equation. The proof becomes the two mathematical steps, congruence on a neighbourhood and then trace commuting with differentiation, without a duplicated expression to keep in sync with the goal.

evidence.excerpt:
lemma wderiv_congr {f g : V n → ℂ} {z : V n} (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z] g) (a : ℂ) (v : V n) :
    wderiv a v f z = wderiv a v g z
def dzbar (v : V n) (f : V n → ℂ) : V n → ℂ := wderiv Complex.I v f

findings.problem: The same `K.isOpen.mem_nhds hz` and `K.smooth.contDiffAt (K.isOpen.mem_nhds hz)` are re-typed several times inside single terms, in connection_smooth, logDet_smooth, curvature_formula and ricciHessian_trace. The determinant-nonvanishing function `fun y hy => ne_of_gt (K.positive y hy).det_pos` is also written out in inverse_smooth (line 43) and curvature_formula (line 77). This hides the structure of the proofs, which is: local smoothness of the matrix at z, then combining.
findings.proposed_change: In connection_smooth, after `intro z hz`, add `have hs := K.smooth.contDiffAt (K.isOpen.mem_nhds hz)` and write `exact matrix_smooth_mul (K.inverse_smooth.contDiffAt (K.isOpen.mem_nhds hz)) (mderiv_smooth hs _ _)`. Do the same in logDet_smooth, using `hs` in `determinant_smooth.contDiffAt.comp z hs`. This is what curvature_formula already does with `hs` on line 73, though it then fails to use `hs` consistently on line 75. Optionally add a small lemma `det_ne_zero (hy : y ∈ K.domain) : (K.matrix y).det ≠ 0 := ne_of_gt (K.positive y hy).det_pos` and use `K.det_ne_zero` in inverse_smooth and curvature_formula.
findings.benefit: Each proof names the one local fact it uses and reuses it, so the argument is shorter and the repeated neighbourhood plumbing disappears. Naming the determinant fact also documents why the inverse is smooth.
